To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) office BP is a poor predictor of target organ damage in children with CNI; 2) 24-hour ABPM is a good predictor of target organ disease; 3) nighttime BP is an important predictor of target organ injury in children with CCI; and 4) 24-hour SBP is the only significant predictor of LVH in children with CCRF.

(a) office blood pressure measurements are not reliable in children with chronic kidney disease (CKD), and (b) ambulatory blood pressure measurements are better predictors for target organ damage in children with CKD than office blood pressure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between blood pressure and left ventricular mass in children with chronic kidney disease.
the evaluation of the blood pressure profile in children with chronic kidney disease.
the prevalence and clinical correlates of hypertension in children with chronic kidney disease (CKD).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the prevalence of hypertension is higher using ABPM than casual blood pressure in children and adolescents with CRI.
ambulatory blood pressure measurement in children is a useful tool to identify hypertension, to assess its severity, and to predict cardiovascular risk.
ambulatory blood pressure is a useful and accurate method of assessing hypertension in children with chronic kidney disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the prevalence of hypertension was higher when using ABPM criteria.
ABPM may help to better define hypertension in children with CNI and may help in the prediction of target organ damage.
ABPM is superior to casual BP in detecting blood pressure abnormalities in children with CNI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ambulatory blood pressure is an important tool to assess hypertension and to identify children with target organ damage.
ambulatory blood pressure measurement is more sensitive than office blood pressure measurement for the detection of hypertension and target organ damage in patients with chronic kidney disease.
ambulatory blood pressure measurement (ABPM) is more useful than casual blood pressure measurement in detecting hypertension and predicting end-organ damage.
